summary: Meta researchers introduce WaiT, a frequency-aware flow-matching image (and video) generation architecture that decomposes generation into coarse and fine wavelet bands, reporting state-of-the-art FID/FVD results and up to 50% reduction in sampling compute.

mechanisms.reason: The paper states a specific technique (frequency-aware wavelet decomposition) that reduces sampling compute needed to generate images at comparable or better quality.
mechanisms.quote: reducing sampling compute by up to 50%

practices.reason: The wavelet-based frequency scheduling technique could reduce sampling compute in diffusion/flow-matching pipelines, but is demonstrated only on the authors' own architecture and models.
practices.quote: reducing sampling compute by up to 50%

practices.reason: The paper proposes a stricter three-axis evaluation protocol at native resolution that could change how image generation quality is measured beyond standard FID.
practices.quote: we introduce a more stringent three-axis evaluation protocol to assess quality at native resolution
